author: Jerdon, 1839
habitat: 바닷가 섬, 키 큰 풀이 우거진 초원과 갈대밭
summary: 우리나라에서는 2003년 12월 25일 신안 대흑산도에서 센 바람이 분 뒤 갓 죽은 채 발견된 것이 첫 기록인 길잃은새이다. 키 큰 풀이 우거진 초원과 갈대밭에 살며, 해 질 녘 풀밭 위를 낮고 조용히 날며 들쥐 같은 작은 포유류를 주로 잡고 개구리와 곤충도 먹는다. 둥지는 땅 위 키 큰 풀숲에 풀을 깔아 만든다. 인도와 중국 남동부, 대만, 동남아시아를 거쳐 뉴기니와 오스트레일리아까지 띄엄띄엄 분포한다.

art.subject: Eastern Grass Owl (Tyto longimembris), adult: heart-shaped facial disc whitish to pale buff, framed by a thin dark rim; small black eyes; crown, nape, back and wing coverts dark brown, finely spotted pale, with golden-buff showing through in patches; flight feathers barred dark; underparts pale buff to whitish with sparse small dark spots; very long legs, the upper part of the tarsus feathered whitish and the lower part and the toes bare and pale. Bill pale.
art.pose: standing upright on a flattened tussock in tall grass, front-side view with the facial disc turned towards the viewer
art.scene: Tall dry grassland and reedbed on a Korean river floodplain at dusk in autumn; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, standing upright on a flattened grass tussock, three-quarter front view: pale heart-shaped facial disc with a dark rim, dark eyes, pale bill, dark brown crown, back and wing coverts with golden-buff markings and pale speckles, buff breast with little streaking, whitish belly, very long legs

adult, standing in tall grass, side view: large rounded head without ear tufts, pale heart-shaped facial disc with a dark rim, dark brown upperparts with golden-buff markings and pale speckles, buff underparts, very long pale legs
art.build: Medium-sized owl with a large rounded head without ear tufts, its body about the size of a pigeon's; long legs; long wings that at rest extend clearly beyond the short tail. In flight the long legs and feet project beyond the tail tip; the upperwing is dark brown with golden-buff bases to the primaries, and the pale underwing has a dark patch at the carpal joint and dark-barred wingtips. Hunts by quartering low over tall grass at dusk; roosts and nests on the ground.
avoid: Do not paint yellow or orange eyes or short ear tufts (Short-eared Owl, Asio flammeus).
Do not paint the pale golden-grey upperparts and white underparts of Barn Owl (Tyto alba); the Grass Owl's upperparts are dark brown.
Do not paint a round face; the facial disc is heart-shaped.
Do not put it in a tree; it lives on the ground in tall grass.
